title: Morning Edition
dek: The UN's warming warning; technology in environmental crime; Europe's energy resilience; and a small Texas craft fair.

lead_story.headline: UN warns climate pledges still point to dangerous warming
lead_story.summary: The UN Environment Programme's latest assessment says even full implementation of current pledges would leave the world heading toward roughly 2.6°C warming by 2100. A 1.5°C pathway without significant overshoot is no longer considered realistic in the report.
lead_story.why_it_matters: The difference between pledged and delivered emissions cuts determines infrastructure, food, health and adaptation decisions for decades.

items.headline: Latin American rights body warns criminal groups are weaponizing connectivity
items.summary: The Inter-American human-rights system's environmental-rights office says drones, satellite internet and online platforms are helping illegal miners and loggers operate in remote regions. It calls for safeguards without cutting communities off from useful technology.
items.why_it_matters: Digital infrastructure can empower conservation and organized crime simultaneously; oversight must distinguish users and harms.

items.headline: Europe's central bank credits cleaner energy and investment for economic resilience
items.summary: ECB economists argue reduced oil dependence, fiscal spending and AI-related trade helped the euro area weather an energy shock better than expected. They caution that some supports may be temporary.
items.why_it_matters: The analysis shows how changes in energy systems can affect economic exposure to conflict-driven price shocks.

items.headline: World weather agency warns of potentially exceptional El Niño
items.summary: WMO chief Celeste Saulo says the developing El Niño could become the strongest in four decades, bringing heightened risks of altered rainfall and heat. The eventual intensity remains a forecast.
items.why_it_matters: Seasonal climate signals influence crop planning, water management and disaster preparation far beyond the Pacific.

items.headline: European lawmakers move to weaken future vehicle-emissions targets
items.summary: Negotiators in the European Parliament reached a compromise lowering proposed 2035 car-emissions reductions and allowing certain credits. The agreement is not yet final EU law.
items.why_it_matters: The shift reveals the tension between industrial policy and climate targets in a major car market.

items.headline: Older catch-up: hurricane attribution study separates warming from El Niño
items.summary: A rapid attribution analysis of Hurricane Polo estimated human-caused warming contributed more to peak winds than El Niño. The analysis was not yet peer reviewed.
items.why_it_matters: Attribution work can distinguish long-term warming from short-term climate variability, but estimates carry methodological uncertainty.

items.headline: Plainview's annual craft festival brings together 47 local vendors
items.summary: The Running Water Draw Arts & Craft Festival drew about 1,500 shoppers to Plainview's Ollie Liner Center. The Rotary-organized weekend featured handmade goods and raised funds for local projects.
items.why_it_matters: A small picture of a town making things, meeting neighbors and supporting its own institutions.

items.headline: A good skeptic needs more than doubt and less than certainty
items.summary: An Aeon essay revisits ancient Academic skepticism, especially Carneades and Cicero, to argue that practical judgment can rely on graded plausibility without pretending to certainty.
items.why_it_matters: It offers a useful alternative to both dogmatic conviction and paralysis: act on reasons while remaining corrigible.

worth_your_time.headline: Inside the Hungarian intellectual network that inspired parts of the American right
worth_your_time.summary: Brian Goodman's reported essay follows the Danube Institute and the postliberal movement around Viktor Orbán, examining what Hungary's 2026 change of government means for a political model that attracted American admirers.
worth_your_time.why_it_matters: The piece distinguishes the electoral defeat of a patron from the endurance of the ideas and institutions that benefited from his rule.
